futures are traded on very thin volume and don't necessarily represent what the markets will do when open.  Watch the first hour and last hour of the market day, but also keep in mind that many bear markets will have rallies only to suck in the "dumb" money before continuing their selloffs.  These bear market rallies can last days or even weeks.   Watch the bond market closely.....equity markets ask "how much can I make" while the bond market asks "how much can I loose", and it is this late  point that is most important given the amount of debt around the A.I. trade.

It gets better they've used these things called SPV Special purpose vehicles to hide the debt from their normal balance sheets. They also use something called ARR Annual recurring revenue where you take one month and simply extrapolate it out and call that your revenue. The problem with CoreWeave isn't that they don't have contracts to cover what they are doing.  They do.  But these are FIXED priced contracts.  Even IF (and that is a big IF) all of these contracts are fulfilled, CoreWeave still has to finance the building of the capacity to fulfill these contracts.  That is where the BIG problems arise.  Since these are FIXED priced contracts, if they don't get the financiing right (for example, they have to borrow money at 15% because of a lack of confidence in their business by lenders and bond holders), then these deals quickly go upside-down and CoreWeave goes bankrupt.  Now, what happens is these bondholders (and banks) aren't 100% confident that CoreWeave will pay their debt so what they do is reinsure the debt on the Secondary Market.  And what it costs to insure that debt has spiked to levels we haven't seen since the 2008 Financial Crisis.  In fact, CoreWeaves debt insurance is priced higher than what Bear Stearns, Lehman Brothers, and WAMU's debt insurance was going for back then and all of these companies collapsed in a matter of days after that happened.
